{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABYs5vVQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhCRyYA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 37, "title": "Add bounded current-object ReferenceNode position/vec3 round-trip support", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 default plugins support current-object `ModelNode` scopes (#21), a scalar `UserDataNode` subset (#31), and the current-renderer exposure reference (#35). Ordinary `ReferenceNode` is still unsupported. In Three.js r186, `reference('position', 'vec3')` with no explicit object uses `state.object.position` (the **rendered object's local** position), which is not the same as `ModelNode('position')` (world position).

glTF already transports node-local transforms, so a tightly constrained *current-rendered-Mesh* position reference may be supported without a new binding registry or extension schema. But glTF transforms may be emitted as either TRS or a matrix and native GLTFLoader can create wrapper Groups, primitive children and clones. A graph-only round trip is insufficient to prove the source and imported **render object** have the same local position.

## Expected outcome

1. **Audit the actual Three.js r186/current installed implementation** before editing:
   - `ReferenceNode` constructor/selector/type semantics, `updateReference(state)`, `getValueFromReference()`, the lazy internal uniform, `NodeFrame` updates, inherited `getSerializeChildren()` / serialize/deserialize, and native GLSL/WGSL handling.
   - GLTFExporter `processNodeAsync()` and transform serialization (`matrixAutoUpdate`, matrix vs translation/rotation/scale, `trs` option), and GLTFLoader node/mesh reconstruction, primitive expansion, caching, cloned material/object ownership and local transform restoration.
   - Relevant existing plugin validation and material-fallback hooks; review the current material/model reference and UserDataNode audits. Identify the exact transform/scene shapes where source and imported local positions really match.
2. Implement minimal **paired, data-only default** serialization/resolution for ordinary, exact native `ReferenceNode` instances with **only**:
   - `property === 'position'`, `uniformType === 'vec3'`, one nonnested property segment;
   - `object === null`, `count === null`, default group/name/base/update behavior, and no external reference/identity;
   - an audited ordinary triangle **Mesh actually used as the render object**, initially restricting to safe single-primitive meshes and transform encodings whose local position survives native glTF export/import unchanged.
   Use real Three.js `ReferenceNode` objects; preserve native per-object position reads and lazy uniforms. The node args carry only the validated selector/type and any demonstrably necessary native constructor state, **never a snapshot of the position or an object reference**. Do not substitute a `ModelNode` or a constant.
3. Validate **every Mesh using the material** on both sides, including distinct meshes sharing a material, geometry/material clones and multiple loaded scenes where proven. Check native source node transforms and the actually exported glTF node definitions as needed; on import check exact node/primitive-to-render-Mesh association, ownership and finite local components. Do not infer ownership from matching names or values. Account for transform normalization, negative zero, non-TRS/sheared matrices, pivots, skinning, instancing, morph/primitive expansion and wrappers by either demonstrating faithful behavior in tests or **explicitly deferring them**. The initial allowlist must prioritize correctness over coverage.
4. Support both unbuilt and legitimately native-built reference instances if their constructor semantics and cache/uniform state can be validated safely. Runtime `reference`/uniform caches may contain Meshes and Vector3 objects and must **never** be traversed as portable graph inputs, snapshotted or invoked via app callbacks. Native update scheduling must continue to select the current rendered object, including after mutating `mesh.position` or switching between meshes with a shared material.
5. Reject unsupported/ambiguous variants explicitly: foreign/non-null `object`, arbitrary or nested selectors, other types, buffers/arrays/textures, extra child links, callbacks, custom groups/names/schedules, unknown meaningful own state, masquerading subclasses, missing/nonfinite/mismatched transforms, or an incompatible render-object association. A separate consumer-owned binding-ID adapter may be documented for foreign objects, **not** silently installed as a default.
6. Preserve Draft v2.0's **all-or-nothing** behavior. Malformed import args/links/references, cycles, invalid unreachable node definitions, failed object ownership or transform checks must retain the **complete ordinary glTF material** with its supported other material extensions, primitive clones and dependency caches. No partly applied TSL entrypoints. Invalid source graphs must fail export explicitly before returning a misleadingly valid asset.
7. Preserve the existing Draft v2.0 schema, `materialType`, ordinary glTF properties/extensions, shared TSL singleton identity and removal of v1.0 support. No user code/GLSL/WGSL or live objects in the file; no Three.js core edits unless existing hooks are shown insufficient. Reuse existing node adapters/validation and renderer-owned generation rather than adding a generic binding framework.

## Context and reproduction

- [Draft v2.0 specification](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [Default node coverage (ReferenceNode deferred)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md)
- [Current-object ModelNode and reference audit](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/reference-node-support.md)
- [Current-object UserDataNode binding/primitive audit (#31)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/user-data-node-support.md)
- [Current-renderer reference audit (#35)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/renderer-reference-node-support.md)
- [Exporter plugin and hooks](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/THREEMaterialsTSLExporterPlugin.ts)
- [Loader plugin and hooks](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/THREEMaterialsTSLLoaderPlugin.ts)
- [Three.js r186 ReferenceNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/ReferenceNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 GLTFExporter](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/examples/jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js)
- [Three.js r186 GLTFLoader](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js)
- [Real demo integration tests](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)

Representative case: an ordinary single-primitive Mesh uses `reference('position', 'vec3')` in a supported NodeMaterial expression. The Mesh has a nonzero local position and may be parented under another transformed object. Two GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader cycles should preserve the *local* (not world) position and native live per-object updates. A matrix/wrapper/primitive layout that retargets the reference must reject or remain deferred, not silently change the meaning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document the audited installed/current Three.js source behavior, exact safe local-transform and single-primitive ownership contract, fixed selector/type/base-state allowlist, and source-level deferral paths.
- [ ] Implement paired default `ReferenceNode('position', 'vec3')` support in existing exporter/loader paths using native Three.js objects. Keep built/unbuilt and runtime-cache handling safe; preserve independence from ModelNode and explicit foreign references.
- [ ] Add **real** GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader integration tests (JSON glTF plus representative GLB) for legitimate nonzero local positions, parent transforms, shared materials with different Mesh positions, graph identity/entrypoints, ordinary material values and supported other glTF material extensions. Assert the **actual rendered Mesh** local position and association in both imports, not merely serialized node JSON.
- [ ] Check native `NodeFrame` position updates before/after import, per-object isolation, mutation and relevant GLSL/WGSL setup/analyze/generate and uniform flow. Distinguish CPU builder/update tests from actual browser/GPU validation.
- [ ] Add strict negative export/import tests for foreign objects, wrong selector/type, custom state/callbacks/groups, missing or mismatched node transforms, nonfinite values, unsafe matrices/wrappers, multi-primitive ownership, invalid links/fields/unreachable definitions/cycles; verify complete **ordinary material fallback** (including other extensions and clones).
- [ ] Update `docs/tsl-node-coverage.md`, affected loader/exporter READMEs, and a focused audit with exact supported/deferred variants and actual validation results. Do not change the Draft v2.0 schema/spec or add generic binding infrastructure.
- [ ] Run and report full `npm --prefix packages/demo test`, package-local loader/exporter builds, demo typecheck/build and `git diff --check`, including failures, warnings, skips and unperformed checks honestly. No root-wide invented test script.

## Optional validation

Browser WebGL/WebGPU visual smoke tests with live local-position updates and different parent transforms. If not run, report that native NodeFrame/shader tests do not establish hardware compilation, uploads or rendered pixels.

## Required post-merge verification

None. **No npm publication or package version bump in this issue.** The maintainer handles releases manually.
